# GPU Whisper Server — First Release

Status: Draft

Depth: Deep
Active profiles: core, backend, operations, security

This specification defines one result: an OpenWhispr/whisper.cpp-based service packaged as a Docker image and deployable through Helm on an existing NVIDIA-enabled Kubernetes cluster. It includes model selection, three memory policies, and HTTP model warmup/unload operations. It authorizes specification work only.

The decision journal is the authoritative source-to-requirement link map. Configurable operating defaults and the minimal bootstrap model are explicitly recorded assumptions; they are not measured performance guarantees. No image build, GPU execution, or Kubernetes deployment has been performed during specification authoring.

## Evidence and terminology

The inspected upstream revision is `6ac14546046ffb17d144a08bcad65337e535cf5`. This identifies research evidence; each implementation release must record the exact upstream revision it packages.

Verified source facts:

- The upstream HTTP example loads one model on startup and has a model replacement route. It has no model unload route or API authentication check. See [server initialization](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/whisper.cpp/blob/6ac14546046ffb17d144a08bcad65337e535cf5/examples/server/server.cpp#L717-L731) and [load/health routes](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/whisper.cpp/blob/6ac14546046ffb17d144a08bcad65337e535cf5/examples/server/server.cpp#L1163-L1215).
- The public API supports initialization from a memory buffer and freeing a complete context. See [public API](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/whisper.cpp/blob/6ac14546046ffb17d144a08bcad65337e535cf5/include/whisper.h#L203-L271) and [context release](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/whisper.cpp/blob/6ac14546046ffb17d144a08bcad65337e535cf5/src/whisper.cpp#L3861-L3875). This does not establish actual runtime memory reclamation.
- The upstream Dockerfile uses CUDA 13.0 and a specific architecture list, while the backend supports a wider architecture set with suitable toolchains. See [CUDA Dockerfile](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/whisper.cpp/blob/6ac14546046ffb17d144a08bcad65337e535cf5/.devops/main-cuda.Dockerfile#L1-L28), [backend architecture selection](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/whisper.cpp/blob/6ac14546046ffb17d144a08bcad65337e535cf5/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/CMakeLists.txt#L8-L55), and [CUDA 13 architecture restrictions](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.0.0/cuda-toolkit-release-notes/index.html#deprecated-architectures).

`RAM` means host memory. `VRAM` means GPU memory. A memory location describes model-owned allocations; a GPU-resident model may also require host allocations. Disk-cached model files are separate from RAM/VRAM residency. A service instance is one running container; its model state and queue are local to that instance.

## Product and platform contract

### REQ-001: One packaged service

The release must provide a buildable Docker image definition, a Helm chart, and instructions for configuration, building, installation, verification, upgrade, rollback, and removal. Docker parameters and Helm values must express the same model and lifecycle behavior. The inference algorithms and model formats remain those of the packaged upstream project; implementing a new speech recognition engine is excluded.

Acceptance: the documented Docker and Helm examples can serve the same configured model and exercise all three memory policies plus warmup/unload. A chart-only scaffold, image-only result, or static server without the agreed lifecycle is insufficient.

### REQ-002: Supported environments and inherited GPU compatibility

Build and runtime target Linux amd64. The build must not require a GPU on the builder. Runtime requires an NVIDIA GPU and a host driver/container integration compatible with the selected CUDA toolchain. No ARM, Windows-container, macOS-container, CPU-only fallback, or distributed multi-GPU inference support is required.

NVIDIA architecture coverage must preserve the CUDA backend coverage of the packaged upstream source revision. Copying a narrower upstream Docker architecture list is insufficient. Toolchain/image variants are permitted if necessary to preserve that coverage, with an explicit mapping of architectures to image variants and driver requirements. Capacity constraints are separate: GPU support does not promise that every model fits every GPU.

The initial Kubernetes matrix is the maintained branches 1.35, 1.36, and 1.37. Helm 3 and Helm 4 must both work with compatible versions: the initial reference minors are Helm 3.22 and 4.3. Exact tested patches must be recorded for the release. Later versions require verification before extending the published matrix; older releases are not required. See [Kubernetes releases](https://kubernetes.io/releases/), [Helm 3 compatibility](https://helm.sh/docs/v3/topics/version_skew/), and [Helm 4 compatibility](https://helm.sh/docs/topics/version_skew/).

The existing cluster supplies the NVIDIA driver, container runtime integration, and device plugin. The chart does not install or configure this infrastructure. An Ingress controller and storage provisioner are external prerequisites when their corresponding features are enabled.

Acceptance: release evidence identifies the source/toolchain/driver/architecture matrix and tests chart compatibility on the declared Kubernetes/Helm combinations. An actual transcription shows CUDA execution on a supported NVIDIA GPU. CPU execution, GPU visibility alone, and assumed compatibility from a successful build do not establish this criterion. Unsupported environments fail clearly rather than being reported as supported.

### REQ-003: Configuration semantics and defaults

Both Docker configuration and Helm values must expose: the model catalog; independently selected download and served model sets; model sources and cache storage; a global memory policy and per-model overrides; per-model automatic warmup settings; GPU selection; server address/port; queue/input/deadline limits; and shutdown/provisioning limits. Helm additionally exposes image identity, scheduling, resources, storage, Service, and Ingress settings.

Model IDs are nonempty ASCII identifiers containing letters, digits, dot, underscore, or hyphen, beginning with a letter or digit, with a maximum length of 128 characters. IDs must be unique. Served and download sets may only reference declared catalog entries. At least one model must be served. An explicit catalog replaces the bootstrap catalog instead of silently retaining its entries. A request cannot change configuration or supply a model URL/filesystem path.

Docker precedence is explicit command-line parameters, then environment settings, then a supplied declarative configuration, then defaults. Collection overrides replace the corresponding collection. Helm retains its standard values precedence and translates the resulting settings to the same validated service contract. Changes to configuration require a restart/Helm upgrade; runtime warmup/unload changes residency, not the configured policy or catalog. Unknown settings, malformed values, duplicate IDs, inconsistent model sets, invalid modes, and invalid limits fail with a bounded diagnostic before serving requests.

The assumed bootstrap catalog serves the multilingual upstream `base` model and downloads it from an official, release-pinned artifact source. It is an example/default, not a restriction on configured upstream models or a recognition-quality guarantee. The confirmed default memory policy is `ram-cache`. Automatic startup warmup is disabled by default. The default server port is 8080; the container listens on its network interface so a published port/Service can reach it.

Assumed, configurable operating defaults:

| Setting | Default | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Active GPU operations per instance | 1 | Fixed first-release invariant |
| Waiting operation capacity | 16 | Integer >= 0; excludes the active operation |
| Uploaded audio size | 25 MiB | Positive; measured on the audio file payload |
| Prompt size | 8 KiB | Positive; measured as UTF-8 bytes |
| Decoded audio duration | 900 seconds | Positive; checked with bounded decoding |
| Operation deadline | 600 seconds | Positive; includes queue wait and execution |
| Cleanup deadline | 10 seconds | Positive; bounds resource-release/recovery handling |
| Graceful shutdown deadline | 30 seconds | Positive; Kubernetes grace must also accommodate cleanup |
| Model provisioning deadline | 1800 seconds | Positive; total bound per provisioning operation |
| Download attempts | 3 | Positive integer; all attempts fit the provisioning deadline |

These bounds are not latency/throughput service-level objectives. They can be raised for an intended workload without changing the mode, isolation, or memory-release guarantees.

Acceptance: equivalent Docker/Helm inputs produce equivalent effective model policies; explicit overrides do not retain an unintended bootstrap model. Conflicting inputs demonstrate the stated precedence. Each invalid configuration above produces a configuration failure, not ignored settings or a partially configured ready service.

## Model artifacts and lifecycle

### REQ-004: Downloaded and served model sets

Operators must be able to choose which catalog models are downloaded and which are available for serving. These are distinct sets: a model may be downloaded without being exposed, and a served model may use an operator-prepared file without downloading. A served model must have a declared source and compatible Whisper model artifact. Arbitrary models outside the served set are not callable, even if a matching file exists in the cache.

Supported sources are release-pinned public HTTPS artifacts and existing files in operator-configured mounted storage. Automatic provisioning prepares the selected download set at startup and reuses valid cached artifacts. Existing-file mode must work without internet access. A configured source may be changed only through configuration, not a transcription/management request.

Acceptance: two configured model IDs select two different actual model artifacts; a download-only ID is rejected by the API. A valid prepopulated cache permits an offline restart without HTTP download traffic, observed at the source/network boundary. A missing existing-file model produces a clear provisioning failure rather than an unexpected download or silent model substitution.

### REQ-005: Cache integrity and ownership

Downloads must have pinned artifact identity and an expected checksum. Existing files may declare a checksum; when supplied it is enforced. Newly downloaded data becomes a reusable cache entry only after successful complete download and integrity verification. Interrupted, truncated, checksum-mismatched, or otherwise invalid artifacts cannot be served as completed cache entries.

Provisioning is bounded by REQ-003, cleans its incomplete output, and preserves previously valid files on failure. Shared cache writers must not publish a partial file or corrupt another valid artifact. Operator-provided existing files are read-only to the service. Model unload and request cleanup never delete disk-cached weights. Upgrade/removal behavior is defined in REQ-017.

Acceptance: interrupted/checksum-failing downloads leave no reusable partial entry and no accumulating incomplete files across retries; a later valid attempt recovers. Cached artifact identity/checksum remains unchanged across warmup, unload, transcription, and pod restart. A cache-hit restart is distinguished from a download by source access observations, not by a success log alone.

### REQ-006: One managed model and safe switching

An instance may own weights for only one managed model ID in RAM/VRAM at a time and may execute only one GPU operation at a time. Downloaded disk files do not count as resident weights. Selecting another model releases the previous model's RAM cache and GPU model allocations before acquiring the new model's weights. Switching is serialized with transcription and management operations; it cannot free a context used by an active request.

If a new load fails after the old model has been released, the instance reports the new model's failure and has no active replacement. It must not serve the old model as if it were the requested model. A subsequent valid request may recover. No guarantee is made that the previous model remains resident after a failed switch.

Acceptance: alternating two model IDs shows at most one managed model's weights and one GPU operation. A queued switch cannot change an in-flight transcription's model. A deliberately invalid replacement reports failure and leaves no hidden second model or mislabeled transcription; a following valid model can be loaded.

### REQ-007: Three per-model memory policies

Each served model inherits the global `ram-cache` default or overrides it with one of the following policies. Policies describe the state after an admitted transcription starts processing, including recoverable request failure/cancellation when model weights remain valid. Rejection during validation, queue overflow, and timeout/cancellation while waiting do not change existing residency or a warmup override:

| Policy | While processing | After processing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resident` | GPU model context is used | The current model remains GPU-resident, with necessary host allocations, until a model switch, explicit unload, or shutdown |
| `ram-cache` | GPU model context is used | GPU model/inference allocations are released; reusable weights for the same model remain in RAM |
| `on-demand` | Weights/context exist only for processing, except the explicit warmup override in REQ-009 | Model-owned RAM and VRAM allocations are released; verified files remain on disk |

In `ram-cache`, a repeated request for the same managed model must reuse RAM weights without rereading its model file. The GPU context/weights may need to be recreated/transferred for each request; no claim of zero transfer time is made. RAM caching is for the last managed model only, not a multi-model cache or an eviction algorithm.

Request-specific audio, prompts, decoder history, and output buffers are never part of retained model weights and must be cleaned/reset independently of policy. A corrupt or unusable context is released rather than retained under `resident`.

Acceptance: real GPU transcriptions exercise all three rows and their cleanup paths. A second same-model RAM-cache request succeeds using cached weights when further model-file reads are prevented. Switching IDs causes a fresh load and releases the previous RAM weights. A later request in `on-demand` reloads weights. Retained audio/decoder history, a second RAM-cached model, or resident GPU model allocations in idle `ram-cache` are excluded by allocation/I/O observations and REQ-018.

### REQ-008: Automatic warmup settings

For each model, an optional automatic startup warmup target is `ram` or `vram`; disabled is the default. Warmup means loading weights into the selected location, not performing synthetic transcription. Automatic warmups follow catalog order, share the one-managed-model invariant, and complete before readiness. If several models are warmed, only the last remains resident; earlier ones may be evicted by subsequent warmups. A failed configured startup warmup prevents ready state and gives a model-specific diagnostic.

Acceptance: enabled startup warmup produces the requested residency before ready state; disabled warmup does not load weights merely because probes are called. Multiple enabled warmups show the specified order and final single-model state. No test inference is performed by warmup, observed at the inference-call boundary.

### REQ-009: HTTP warmup with explicit target

`POST /v1/models/{model}/warmup` accepts JSON `{"target":"ram"}` or `{"target":"vram"}` for a served model. The target is required; missing/invalid/unknown fields produce 400 without mutating residency. The method is serialized with transcriptions and other mutations.

`ram` loads reusable weights into RAM and retains no GPU model allocation. `vram` loads the GPU model context and required host allocations. Both leave the requested weights resident after a successful response, without running transcription. Repeating the same successful model/target warmup is idempotent: it does not duplicate allocations.

An explicit warmup overrides idle residency even for `on-demand`. It does not change the model's configured serving policy. The override lasts until the next completed processing of that model applies REQ-007, another model is selected, explicit unload occurs, or the instance stops. Automatic warmup has the same temporary-residency semantics. A response acknowledges completed loading, not merely queued work, and returns JSON fields `model`, `state` (`ram` or `vram`), and `mode` (the configured policy).

Acceptance: warm an on-demand model in each target, observe persistence after the HTTP response, then transcribe and observe full cleanup. Invalid/unserved model IDs return 404 without releasing a different current model. Repeated warmup shows unchanged allocation ownership rather than accumulating memory. GPU-load failure cannot return a successful VRAM-resident state.

### REQ-010: HTTP unload

`POST /v1/models/{model}/unload` accepts an empty body or an empty JSON object for a served model. Unknown body fields are invalid. It serializes with the active operation and releases that model's RAM weights and GPU model/inference allocations. It does not interrupt an active transcription, delete files, remove a model from the served set, or change its policy.

The method is idempotent. An already unloaded served model returns 200 with JSON fields `model`, `state: "unloaded"`, and `mode`. Unloading a model other than the current managed model leaves the current model untouched. A later queued/new transcription may load the model again; unload acknowledges the state at its serialized completion, not a permanent ban on future loading.

Acceptance: explicit unload returns only after REQ-018 is met for the selected model. Repeating it succeeds without extra side effects. An unload queued during transcription cannot invalidate that transcription. Unserved IDs return 404 and leave current residency and disk files unchanged. No restart is needed for a subsequent successful transcription.

### REQ-011: Queue, deadlines, and cancellation

Transcription, warmup, and unload share a first-in-first-out queue, with at most one active mutation/GPU operation and the waiting capacity in REQ-003. Validation failures do not occupy the queue or mutate model state. Queue overflow returns 429. Its error declares that the rejected operation was not executed and may be retried. A zero waiting capacity allows an idle instance to execute one operation and rejects work while busy.

An operation's deadline starts at admission and includes waiting and execution. A waiting operation that expires returns 408 if its connection is usable and never loads/unloads a model. An expired active operation or observed client cancellation stops work safely, applies cleanup/policy, and releases the queue before reuse. No resources are freed while still in use. If safe cleanup cannot finish within its deadline, the instance becomes unready and terminates for restart instead of admitting another operation against uncertain state.

An unobserved client disconnect cannot extend work past the operation deadline. Network/process loss may prevent delivery of an HTTP error; this is not a promise of exactly-once delivery. Repeated transcription is permitted and has no persisted business side effect. The service does not silently retry completed inference operations.

Acceptance: mixed-model transcription/warmup/unload requests observe FIFO ordering and no overlap. Overflow and waiting timeout never invoke model mutation, verified at the operation/load boundary. Active cancellation/timeout does not poison the next valid request or leak audio/model allocations. Unsafe cleanup takes the unready/restart path, not concurrent reuse.

## HTTP and state contract

### REQ-012: Synchronous transcription API

`POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` accepts `multipart/form-data`. Exactly one `file` and one `model` are required. `model` is a served catalog ID; there is no model fallback, implicit path loading, or unconfigured download. The minimal bootstrap example uses `model=base`; clients must use the configured ID, including in OpenWhispr Self-Hosted settings.

Optional fields are `language` (supported upstream language identifier or `auto`, default `auto`), `prompt` (UTF-8, subject to the configurable byte limit in REQ-003), `temperature` (finite number in [0, 1], default 0), and `response_format` (`json` or `text`, default `json`). Duplicate required/scalar fields, invalid values, and unsupported fields/formats are rejected with 400. `stream=true` is rejected; `stream=false` is accepted as an explicit synchronous request. Language/model incompatibility must be reported instead of silently substituting a different model or ignoring an explicit unsupported language.

The first release accepts WAV, MP3, MP4, MPEG, MPGA, M4A, OGG, FLAC, and WebM input with decodable audio, including WebM/Opus and OGG/Opus browser recordings. These input file families match the [official transcription file contract](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/audio/subresources/transcriptions/methods/create); the response subset remains JSON/text. Content is validated and normalized for the upstream engine; extension/MIME declarations alone are insufficient. Unsupported/corrupt audio or a container without a decodable audio track returns 400. File size above the configured payload bound returns 413, and bounded decoding rejects audio exceeding the configured duration. Multipart framing must allow a file at the configured limit; uploads/decoding cannot consume unbounded memory or temporary storage before rejecting it.

Acceptance: an OpenAI-compatible client and OpenWhispr can send valid batch audio for each advertised format and obtain their configured model's transcript. Malformed multipart, missing/duplicate fields, unknown IDs, unsupported streaming/formats, invalid numeric/language values, oversized upload, and overlong/corrupt decoded audio produce the declared rejection without inference or mutation of another model. Mock/CPU results do not prove GPU operation.

### REQ-013: Results, errors, and request isolation

A successful JSON transcription returns 200, `application/json`, and `{"text":"..."}`. Text format returns 200 and UTF-8 `text/plain`. Warmup/unload return 200 only for their completed acknowledged state. Errors use JSON `{"error":{"message":"...","type":"...","param":null,"code":"..."}}`, with `param` set to an applicable public field when relevant. Error messages are bounded and do not expose paths, secrets, audio, prompts, or transcripts.

The status mapping is: 400 invalid input, 404 unserved model/unknown route, 413 upload bound, 429 full queue, 408 operation deadline, 503 unavailable model/GPU/provisioning or shutdown, and 500 otherwise unrecoverable in-process execution failure. Distinct error codes identify the cause. A provisioning/model-init failure is not mislabeled as successful transcription. A hard process/driver failure may instead terminate a connection and follows REQ-017 recovery.

HTTP-visible compatibility is limited to the declared synchronous transcription subset and the explicit lifecycle extensions. Full OpenAI compatibility, `/v1/models` listing, audio translation API, streaming, and the upstream filesystem-path `/load` interface are not advertised. Unknown routes, including `/load`, must not bypass the configured model catalog.

Each response contains only its own request's result; retained model state cannot carry another request's prompt, transcript, decoder history, language, or output into it. Reuse of weights is permitted. Recoverable request failure leaves the queue/state able to serve a following valid request, unless cleanup requires the specified restart path.

Acceptance: parse success/error bodies with the declared clients; alternate requests with distinct audio/languages/prompts and verify isolation. A malformed request followed by a valid request recovers. Unknown routes and raw path-load attempts return 404 rather than replacing the allowed model. Synthetic warmup output is absent because warmup invokes no inference.

### REQ-014: Health and readiness

`GET /health/live` returns 200 with JSON `{"status":"live"}` for a responsive process independently of the GPU-operation queue. `GET /health/ready` returns 200 with JSON `{"status":"ready"}` when configuration/provisioning and any configured startup warmup are complete, required model artifacts are available, and a compatible GPU backend can be used. Otherwise it returns 503 with a bounded reason, or is unreachable before the HTTP process is listening. Readiness does not imply that every model fits a GPU's memory or that performance has been measured.

An idle on-demand instance can be ready with no resident weights. RAM-cache readiness does not require idle GPU model allocations. Probe calls never load, warm, unload, or transcribe a model, and cannot wait behind long inference. Loss of GPU capability prevents ready state and successful CPU fallback. Model-specific allocation/init errors are reported for that model; recoverable errors do not permanently block unrelated valid work.

Acceptance: probes stay responsive during queued/active work and repeated probes cause no model I/O, inference calls, or residency changes. Cold and RAM-only states are correctly ready after preparation. Missing/broken provisioning, incompatible/unavailable GPU, failed configured startup warmup, and shutdown do not appear ready. GPU listing alone cannot substitute for actual execution evidence.

## Packaging, operations, and privacy

### REQ-015: Container operation

The image contains the upstream-compatible CUDA inference capability and the audio-decoding capability needed by REQ-012, with release metadata identifying the upstream revision and toolchain/runtime identities. Building uses declared immutable source and base-image identities rather than a moving upstream branch as a release identity. Model catalog changes do not require rebuilding the executable image; model weights are supplied/provisioned separately at runtime.

The documented invocation supports Docker parameters/environment configuration, mounted cache/existing models, the selected GPU, network publication, and termination signals. The service runs without administrative/root privileges; writable locations are limited to configured cache and transient work storage. Errors/operational diagnostics use stdout/stderr with meaningful process exit status. Configuration/dependency failure cannot be reported as a running ready service. The container does not require Kubernetes to provide its core API/lifecycle behavior.

Acceptance: a clean GPU-free Linux amd64 builder produces the image; its metadata identifies the declared source/toolchain. A standalone NVIDIA Docker runtime serves transcription and model management with mounted model sources. The process UID/permissions and signal behavior match this contract. A source tree copied into an image or a CUDA compiler installed without a working runtime is insufficient.

### REQ-016: Helm deployment configuration

The chart must install the service with configurable image repository/tag or digest, CPU/RAM requests and limits, persistent cache or an existing claim, read-only existing model mounts, and isolated temporary storage. It requests one `nvidia.com/gpu` resource per instance by default; any explicit GPU request and limit must be equal. Zero allocated GPU is invalid for this service. Node selectors/affinity, tolerations, and an optional runtime class are configurable without installing a runtime/operator.

The default replica count is one. Additional replicas have independent queues/residency and require one available compatible GPU each plus storage supporting the configured mounts. Management operations affect only the addressed instance, not every replica behind a load-balancing Service. Global cache coordination, all-replica warmup/unload, and autoscaling are not required.

The Service is internal by default. Ingress is optional and disabled by default; when enabled it exposes the declared API with configurable host, class, annotations, and TLS references through an existing controller. It does not install a controller, issue certificates, or provide authentication. Public model mutations share the same first-release authorization limitation as transcription.

Startup, readiness, and liveness probes follow REQ-014 and accommodate the configured provisioning/warmup budget. Kubernetes termination grace accommodates shutdown plus cleanup. Invalid values fail validation/rendering rather than yielding a silently degraded manifest. Scheduling without sufficient GPUs may remain pending with Kubernetes events; it must not silently schedule CPU serving.

Acceptance: both Helm majors render/validate and install the declared matrix, using equivalent service settings. Rendered GPU resources/probes/grace/volumes reflect overrides. A GPU cluster installation performs real transcription plus warmup/unload. A second replica demonstrates local state instead of false global management acknowledgments. Ingress-disabled output exposes only Service access; enabled output contains the chosen TLS/controller references and no claimed authorization.

### REQ-017: Shutdown, rollout, and recovery

On termination, the instance becomes unready and stops admitting work. It permits active work to complete within the shutdown deadline, cancels queued work with 503 where possible, and safely cleans model/audio allocations. If active work cannot finish, cancellation and the cleanup/restart rules apply; forced process loss may drop connections. No model is freed concurrently with a still-running operation.

Rollout/rollback must be possible without a spare GPU: the default rollout may stop the old instance before starting its replacement, with documented downtime. Zero-downtime rollout is not promised. New release/configuration failure does not overwrite/delete a previously valid cached artifact. Distinct artifact identities remain distinguishable so rollback can reuse previous valid cache data. A restart begins with empty process-local residency/queue, revalidates configuration and artifacts, and applies configured startup warmup.

Uninstall must not delete/modify an operator-provided claim or files. A chart-owned persistent cache is retained by default; its separate disposal is an explicit operator action. Runtime unload never deletes disk cache. Provisioning interruption, bad model, out-of-memory/init failure, missing GPU, and abrupt process termination have observable diagnostics and a documented recovery path. An in-process model failure returns the specified error and can be retried after correction; a kernel/driver/process kill may lose accepted work and is recovered by restart, not a fabricated HTTP success.

Acceptance: SIGTERM, forced kill, failed rollout, and rollback preserve valid disk artifacts and restore the expected mode after restart. Running/queued requests have the declared completion/cancellation/loss behavior. A single-GPU upgrade can complete instead of waiting forever for a surge GPU. Removal preserves existing storage, with cache retention visible in the remaining claim/files.

### REQ-018: Observable memory reclamation

Successful cleanup means release of model/inference allocations attributable to the requested RAM/VRAM residency, not merely updating a status field. After unload/on-demand completion, no application-owned model weights remain in RAM or VRAM. After RAM-cache completion, only the current reusable RAM weights may remain; model/inference GPU allocations are released. After a model switch, the previous model's RAM/GPU allocations are gone. Temporary/request allocations follow the same ownership rule on every terminal path.

Release occurs within the configured cleanup deadline. Runtime/driver/allocator housekeeping may retain bounded process memory unrelated to model weights; zero total process RSS or zero total GPU memory is not promised. Verification establishes a baseline/envelope on the tested runtime and combines actual CPU/GPU allocation observations with repeated load/use/unload cycles. A declared envelope cannot excuse retaining model-size allocations or sustained growth. Status/log messages alone are insufficient evidence.

Acceptance: two distinct model sizes, each policy, repeated same-model warmups, switches, successful requests, malformed input, cancelled/timed-out requests, and load failures demonstrate the specified reclamation and no accumulating model allocations. The absence checks must be shown to detect suppressed cleanup/model release. CPU RSS, GPU allocation evidence, and model-buffer/I/O observations are retained with the tested environment; claiming memory safety from a health response or mock is excluded.

### REQ-019: First-release access and sensitive data

V1 deliberately has no API authentication/authorization: no required API key, user account, client/operator role, or built-in proxy authentication. Anyone with network access can call transcription, warmup, and unload. This limitation must be stated beside deployment/access instructions; TLS does not change it. The chart's internal-Service/disabled-Ingress defaults do not constitute identity-based authorization. No promise of denied management access or isolation among network users is made.

The service still enforces the configured model catalog, input/resource bounds, and least-privilege container/filesystem boundaries. Model IDs and uploaded filenames cannot become arbitrary filesystem access or shell instructions. Audio is transient: no recordings, prompts, or transcripts are retained as application data. Temporary audio and request buffers are removed/released on success, rejection, conversion failure, cancellation, timeout, and shutdown; an abrupt kill leaves only disposable instance-local transient storage, which cannot be re-served as another request's input and is cleaned on restart/replacement.

Logs contain bounded operational information such as model ID, stage, outcome, and error code; they do not contain uploaded audio, transcript/prompt content, credentials, or client-controlled filenames. Weight source credentials, if present in operator configuration, are not baked into image layers or emitted in diagnostics. Logging can report failure without dumping raw decoder/subprocess output containing sensitive content.

Acceptance: valid calls without Authorization succeed, including model mutations; a first-release role check must not be claimed. Unknown model/path/oversized inputs are rejected despite the absence of identity controls. Inspect logs, transient storage, and request-allocation ownership after success and each failure path with recognizable test markers; sensitive markers must be absent outside the caller's response. No recording/transcript database or retention service is created.

## Completion and future scope

### REQ-020: Objective release evidence

Release verification must include the build and configuration checks, real standalone Docker CUDA transcription, Helm rendering/schema checks for the supported matrix, real Kubernetes GPU installation/transcription, and lifecycle/concurrency/failure/privacy scenarios referenced above. Exercise at least two different compatible model artifacts, one invalid artifact, and all advertised input file families, including the browser Opus encodings. Native inference/model capability remains upstream-owned; tests must target the service's packaging, selection, state, and resource boundaries.

Report source/image/chart identities, model identities, Kubernetes/Helm/toolchain/driver/GPU versions, actual performed checks, failed checks, and unavailable environments. Source inspection, rendering, GPU enumeration, and passing unit tests must not be described as end-to-end GPU or memory evidence. Missing mandatory runtime evidence keeps implementation verification incomplete; it does not change an unrun check into a pass.

Acceptance: evidence traces the public scenarios to observations with their excluded outcomes, including discriminating absence checks for cleanup/probe behavior. No unmet runtime prerequisite is hidden by an Approved specification status. Specification approval means requirements completeness only and does not claim the release has been built or accepted.

### REQ-021: First-release exclusions

Excluded from implementation scope are a new visual UI/admin web server, API authentication/access management, Prometheus exposition, recording/transcript persistence, full OpenAI API/streaming, new inference algorithms, Kubernetes/GPU infrastructure provisioning, automatic publication/CI release infrastructure, distributed model state, multi-model RAM/GPU residency, multi-GPU inference, autoscaling, and unmeasured latency/throughput/recognition-quality guarantees.

The explicit lifecycle HTTP extensions and health endpoints remain included. This is a scope boundary, not authorization to remove upstream library capabilities or cancel the future directions in REQ-022.

Acceptance: the released API/documentation names its supported subset and limitations. No `/metrics`, authentication requirement, administration UI, or distributed-management guarantee is advertised as implemented; route inspection and unauthenticated-call behavior provide observable signals. Packaging and the agreed lifecycle cannot be deferred under these exclusions.

### REQ-022: Development after V1

The specification must keep a separate future-development section identifying:

- Authentication/authorization and issuance/administration of access.
- A possible lightweight web server/admin UI for access management and observing service operation; this is a proposed direction, not a confirmed V1 UI requirement.
- Prometheus metrics for operational visibility.

These directions are retained for later versions. They do not add first-release endpoints, active UI profile/artifacts, implementation steps, dates, estimates, or a commitment to a particular future design. Their detailed contracts require subsequent specification work.

Acceptance: this section contains all three directions with their stated certainty and explicit deferral. Their omission, implementation during V1, or presentation as already delivered is excluded.

Acceptance: each planned contract has an unambiguous behavioral requirement source and preserves the first-release/future boundary. No implementation-local classes/files, task packets, handoff, estimates, or executable solution are introduced by this specification.
